name: 3. Java Backend Development with Spring Boot

quiz.question: In Spring Boot 4.x, which starter dependency is used for traditional Spring MVC REST APIs (replacing the deprecated spring-boot-starter-web)?
options: spring-boot-starter-http
spring-boot-starter-webmvc
spring-boot-starter-servlet-old
spring-boot-starter-tomcat-only
quiz.explanation: In Spring Boot 4.x, spring-boot-starter-webmvc is the standard starter for Spring MVC web applications and REST APIs, replacing spring-boot-starter-web.

quiz.question: What three capabilities does @SpringBootApplication combine?
options: @Entity, @Table, and @Repository
@SpringBootConfiguration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan
@RestController, @Service, and @Transactional
@GetMapping, @PostMapping, and @Valid
quiz.explanation: @SpringBootApplication combines @SpringBootConfiguration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan starting from the root application package.

quiz.question: Why is constructor injection generally preferred over field injection (@Autowired on fields) for required dependencies?
options: Constructor injection makes required dependencies explicit, supports final immutable fields, and simplifies unit testing without starting Spring
Field injection is not supported in Spring Boot 4
Constructor injection automatically connects to PostgreSQL
Field injection prevents HTTP requests from reaching controllers
quiz.explanation: Constructor injection ensures dependencies are explicit, allows final fields, prevents partially initialized objects, and lets unit tests pass mocks directly.

quiz.question: Why should JPA @Entity classes generally NOT be returned directly from REST controller endpoints?
options: Spring MVC cannot serialize Java classes
Returning entities can expose sensitive fields (like passwordHash), couple the API to database structure, and cause lazy-loading serialization issues
Entities cannot have getters
DTOs are required by the JVM compiler
quiz.explanation: Separating JPA entities from request/response DTOs protects sensitive fields, avoids over-posting, prevents lazy-loading serialization problems, and decouples API contracts from DB tables.

quiz.question: What is the role of the DispatcherServlet in Spring MVC?
options: It compiles Java bytecode
It acts as the central front controller/dispatcher that routes incoming HTTP requests via HandlerMapping to controller methods and message converters
It manages PostgreSQL connection pooling
It replaces Maven
quiz.explanation: DispatcherServlet is the central request dispatcher in Spring MVC, coordinating HandlerMapping, controller execution, and HTTP message conversion.

quiz.question: What is the difference between @Component and @Bean in Spring?
options: @Component is placed on a class for component scanning; @Bean is placed on a method inside a @Configuration class to explicitly register the returned object
@Bean is only for controllers; @Component is only for repositories
They are identical
@Component only works for third-party JAR classes
quiz.explanation: @Component marks your own class for component scanning, while @Bean on a @Configuration method registers a returned object (especially useful for third-party library classes).

quiz.question: In application.yml, what does spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto: validate do?
options: Drops and recreates all tables on every restart
Automatically alters production tables when entities change
Checks that the existing database schema matches JPA entity mappings without modifying the schema
Disables SQL queries
quiz.explanation: ddl-auto: validate verifies schema compatibility against entities without mutating tables; production schema changes should use versioned migrations like Flyway or Liquibase.

quiz.question: In Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters), what is a Port and what is an Adapter?
options: A port is a TCP socket; an adapter is a USB cable
A port is an interface defining what the application core needs or exposes; an adapter implements or connects a specific technology (like JPA or REST) to that port
A port is a SQL table; an adapter is a DTO
Both terms refer to Maven plugins
quiz.explanation: Ports define technology-agnostic interfaces at the application core boundary, and adapters (e.g., REST controller or JPA repository adapter) connect external technologies to those ports.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of @RestControllerAdvice in a Spring Boot REST API?
options: To start an embedded Tomcat server
To centralize exception handling across controllers and return consistent error responses (such as 404, 409, or 400 validation errors)
To generate database migrations
To inject dependencies into static methods
quiz.explanation: @RestControllerAdvice centralizes @ExceptionHandler methods so all controllers return a consistent, sanitized error format.

quiz.question: Why should a @Transactional database transaction NOT be held open while calling a slow external email API?
options: Spring Boot forbids @Transactional on services
Holding a DB transaction open during slow network I/O ties up database connections and locks; instead, store an event/outbox record or handle external calls separately
Email APIs cannot run in Java 21
Transactions automatically roll back after 1 millisecond
quiz.explanation: Long-running external I/O inside a DB transaction exhausts connection pools and increases contention; keep DB transactions focused on coherent database operations.
